Subject: Re: MAP cadence and acceptance window

Alex — quick heads up from our side. Legal bumped their review of the data residency appendix and procurement now expects a minimum two-week extension before they can sign off. That pushes our original acceptance window out by ~10 business days.

This is going to compress the planned acceptance run and create risk for our go‑live target (end of Q1). Subject: Re: MAP cadence and acceptance window

Sam — thanks for the heads up and for looping Maria in. I know the team has been working hard to hit the original window; let me propose a pragmatic path forward so we keep momentum without sacrificing acceptance quality.

High level proposal (summary):
- Rebaseline acceptance window by +10 business days (new locked acceptance window: 2027-02-28 to 2027-03-11).
- Add a 2-stage canary: a low-latency traffic slice (week 1) followed by full functional validation (week 2).
- Contingency options: staggered cutover (by customer org) or phased feature flag rollouts.
- Credit proposal: Redwood offers a one‑time service credit (to be negotiated with procurement) if Novus requires a firm go‑live date beyond the new window.

I drafted an updated MAP doc and attached a clean copy for review: novus_map_v2.docx. I also included a short risk ledger in the doc that calls out legal/procurement and contingency triggers.

Quick asks: can Maria confirm the procurement milestones that must be met before signoff? Also looping in Laura and Camila on the Red team for procurement/ops coordination.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Risk ledger (high level):
- Procurement gating milestone (2026-12-08) if missed -> acceptance window shifts another 1–2 weeks.
- Legal clean but billing/KMS key onboarding has dependencies that could slip by 3–5 business days if procurement routes change.
- Executive patience limited; we should be conservative on credits.

3) Ask Karthik for an SLA exception memo if Novus insists on locking the original go‑live date (we need to quantify exposure).

I will own the credit matrix and the telemetry checklist. Camila — can you confirm ops capacity for a staged cutover the week after the acceptance window?

Subject: Proposed MAP rebaseline accepted — actions, contingency, and escalation path

Sam / Maria — thanks for the quick responses and for confirming procurement sequencing. Per our thread and internal alignment, please find the agreed next steps below. This message formalizes the rebaseline and the escalation triggers so procurement and exec sponsors have a single reference.

Agreed (summary):
- Rebaseline: acceptance window moved to 2027-02-28 through 2027-03-11. NOV-7843 MAP v2 attached.
- Canary & validation: Week A (10% traffic slice), Week B (50% then full), telemetry pass required for progression.
- Credit posture: Redwood proposes medium tier credit if budget release slips beyond 2026-12-08 (documented in credit_matrix.xlsx). Final credit terms to be negotiated in a single-line amendment to the MSA.
- Contingency trigger & escalation path: If procurement misses 2026-12-08 by >7 calendar days, Redwood will: (a) enact the staged cutover plan, (b) notify exec sponsors, and (c) open a short-term credit window per the matrix. Karthik will prepare an SLA exposure memo for executive review (cc'd).

Next actions (owners & due dates):
- Maria: confirm procurement milestones and internal signature owner by 2026-11-30.
- Alex: finalize MAP v2 and send to legal (done — attached).
- Laura: deliver telemetry acceptance checklist by 2026-11-27.
- Camila: ops runbook for staged cutover by 2026-12-01.
- Karthik: SLA exposure memo by 2026-11-30.

We will treat this as the canonical MAP for scheduling and escalations. If Novus requires a locked go‑live date earlier than the rebaseline, we should reopen a separate exec-level negotiation.

Thanks — I will update the shared MAP link once Laura and Camila post the runbook/checklist.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
